summary: An excerpt from a novel in which Lexy Moran and Captain Grey talk by the fire about his feelings of uneasiness and a sense of warning, which he finally explains concerns his sister. Lexy encourages him to trust such feelings, and he recounts that his mother died in India when his sister Muriel was born, that Muriel was raised in the States by an aunt, and that the two have not met since he was six and she was a baby. The passage ends with the siblings' long separation of twenty-one years and Lexy's growing interest.
one_line: Lexy Moran listens as Captain Grey confides a troubling premonition about his long-estranged sister Muriel.
key_facts: Lexy Moran and Captain Grey talk together by the firelight, and Lexy studies his face, finding it sensitive and fine rather than haughty.
Captain Grey describes a feeling of uneasiness that something is wrong and asks whether one ought to laugh at it or take it as a warning.
Lexy replies that such feelings are a warning and that it is foolish and wrong to disregard them, even if one's own mind says it is nonsense.
Captain Grey says he has been trying to tell himself he is an utter ass but knew all along that there was something wrong.
Lexy feels an unreasoning dread and for a moment does not want to hear more before agreeing to listen.
Captain Grey's sister is named Muriel.
Captain Grey last saw his sister when he was six years old and she was a baby; they have never met since.
Captain Grey's mother died when Muriel was born, out in India.
An aunt took Muriel to the States, while Captain Grey stayed out there with his father.
The last picture Captain Grey had of Muriel showed her at about fourteen, which he described as lovely.
It was arranged that Muriel would come to England while Captain Grey was at school there, but she did not come.
Captain Grey notes that twenty-one years have passed since they last met, and Muriel is now twenty-one years old.
Lexy's dread disappears once Captain Grey begins talking about his sister, and she feels lively interest in hearing about her.
